ORDER With consent of both the parties, matter is heard finally.

2. This criminal revision under Section 397/401 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by petitioner being aggrieved by the impugned judgment dated 23.12.2011 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Gohad,
District Bhind in Criminal Appeal No.34/2010, whereby judgment and order of conviction dated 11.2.2010 passed by JMFC, Gohad in Criminal Case No.144/2006, by which applicant has been convicted for the offence under Section 498A of IPC and sentenced to undergo one year RI with fine of Rs.2000/-, with usual default stipulation.

entities.text:
Additional Sessions Judge, Gohad,
District Bhind
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Prosecution story in brief is that marriage of the complainant Chandrakanta was solemnized with Ram Bharose Sharma on 20.6.2005 who NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16785 2 CRR-1096-2011 is son of applicant Smt. Urmila Devi and the applicant is mother-in-law of the complainant.

At the time of marriage, parents of the complainant has given T.V., Cooler, Yamaha Motorcycle, Rs.84,000/- cash and jewelery as dowry but after sometime present applicant and Purushottam Sharma who is brother-in-law (Jeth) of the complainant mentally and physically harassed the complainant for non-fulfillment of their demand of Rs.50,000/- cash as dowry.
Applicant also tried to give poison to the complainant.
Complainant Chandrakanta narrated the whole incident to her father thereafter lodged an FIR at Police Station Mehagaon, District Bhind.

Accordingly, offence has been registered.

4. After conclusion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed against the applicant and other co-accused persons before JMFC, Gohad who framed charges under Section 498A of IPC against the applicant and other co- accused persons.
Applicant abjured her guilt and took a plea that she has been falsely implicated in this matter.
Prosecution has examined as many as six witnesses while defence has examined three witnesses.

5. The trial Court after scrutinizing evidence available on record and considering the rival submissions made by both the parties, has convicted and sentenced the applicant under Section 498-A of IPC.
Applicant has filed an appeal before the First Appellate Court but same has been dismissed by affirming the impugned judgment passed by the Trial Court.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, this criminal revision has been preferred before this Court.

6. During pendency of this criminal revision, both the parties filed joint compromise application I.A.No.1519/2020 which has been verified by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16785 3 CRR-1096-2011 the Principal Registrar of this Court and submitted his verification report that both the parties have arrived at compromise voluntarily, without any threat, inducement and coercion but offence under Section 498-A of IPC is not compoundable.
Although the offence is not compoundable but factum of compromise can be considered while sentencing the applicant.

7. Petitioner has preferred this criminal revision on several grounds but during the course of argument, learned counsel for applicant did not press this revision on merit and not assailed the finding part of impugned judgment.

He confines his arguments on the point of sentence only and prays that matter has been amicably settled between both the parties, applicant who is 74 years old,
remained 01 day in custody and suffering trial since last 25 years and she is not having any criminal antecedent, therefore, it is prayed that present revision be disposed of and jail sentence awarded to the applicant be reduced to the period already undergone.
8.
Learned counsel for respondent/State on the other hand supported the impugned judgment and prays for dismissal of this revision.

9. Since petitioner has not challenged the conviction recorded by Courts below, in these circumstances conviction recorded against applicant for the offence under Section 498-A of IPC is hereby affirmed.

However, considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that since applicant has already suffered jail sentence for about 01 day, she is facing trial since 2006 i.e.
about 25 years now, she is aged about 74 years, she is not having any criminal background,
therefore, this Court finds that it would be appropriate to partly allow the revision by affirming the conviction, however, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16785 4 CRR-1096-2011 by reducing her jail sentence to the period already undergone but by enhancing the fine amount from Rs.2000 to Rs.5000/-.
10.

Accordingly, this revision petition is partly allowed by maintaining the conviction, but reducing the jail sentence to the period already undergone by applicant, however, by enhancing fine amount Smt.Urmila vs State Of M.P. on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101470039/
2 under Section 498-A of IPC from Rs.2000 to Rs.5000/-.

Disposal of property shall be conducted as per the order of trial Court.
